title: UK Energy Suppliers Compared: Every Major Firm
description: Compare UK energy suppliers: the largest firms, green specialists, app-based challengers and prepay specialists, plus the E.ON and OVO takeover explained.
intro: Who supplies Britain’s homes, what each type of supplier is known for, and how to check customer service before you switch. No paid rankings, just the facts and links to check.

cardText: Big suppliers, green specialists, challengers and prepay firms.

blocks.title: Supplier cards
blocks.intro: Filter by type. Links go to each supplier’s own website. We don’t rate suppliers: see Citizens Advice’s customer service rankings for that.

items.title: Octopus Energy
items.text: Became Britain’s largest household supplier after taking on Bulb and Shell Energy’s home customers. Known for smart and EV tariffs such as Agile, Go and Tracker.

items.title: British Gas
items.text: The UK’s longest-established home energy brand and still the largest supplier of household gas. Owned by Centrica.

items.title: E.ON Next
items.text: Formed from E.ON UK and npower’s customers. Agreed to buy OVO in 2026: the takeover was cleared by the competition regulator in October and is expected to complete later.

items.title: OVO Energy
items.text: Grew by taking on SSE’s household customers. Being bought by E.ON: OVO says customers will be told well in advance of any change, and existing tariffs will be honoured.

items.title: EDF
items.text: Part of the French state-owned EDF group, which runs Britain’s nuclear power stations. Offers fixed, EV and export tariffs.

items.title: ScottishPower
items.text: Owned by Iberdrola and one of the UK’s biggest wind power developers. Supplies homes across Great Britain, not only Scotland.

items.title: Utility Warehouse
items.text: Bundles energy with broadband, mobile and insurance, with savings for taking more services. Sold through partners rather than price comparison sites.

items.title: So Energy
items.text: Mid-sized independent supplier that took on ESB Energy’s customers. Focus on renewable-backed electricity and simple tariffs.

items.title: Outfox the Market
items.text: Online-only supplier built around low overheads and simple pricing. Check which fuels and tariffs are available at your address.

items.title: Fuse Energy
items.text: App-based newer supplier that also develops its own renewable energy projects.

items.title: Good Energy
items.text: Long-standing green supplier that buys renewable electricity from independent UK generators. Also a big player in feed-in and export payments.

items.title: Ecotricity
items.text: Green energy company founded in 1995 that builds its own wind and solar parks and offers green gas.

items.title: Green Energy UK
items.text: Independent green supplier known for green gas and its TIDE time-of-use electricity tariff.

items.title: Utilita
items.text: Specialises in smart pay-as-you-go energy, topped up by app, online or in shops.

sections.h2: How the UK supplier market looks in 2026
sections.html:
A handful of large companies supply the vast majority of British homes. Octopus Energy is now the largest household supplier, followed by British Gas, E.ON Next, OVO, EDF and ScottishPower. Most of the smaller suppliers that collapsed during the 2021–22 crisis had their customers moved to one of these firms under Ofgem’s “Supplier of Last Resort” process, so you may be with a big supplier without ever having chosen it.

Big news: E.ON has agreed to buy OVO. The deal received competition clearance in early October 2026. Until it completes, the two firms keep operating separately and all existing tariffs are honoured. Read what the E.ON and OVO takeover means for you.

Sources: MoneySavingExpert: E.ON and OVO takeover · Which?: what the takeover means for OVO customers.

sections.h2: How to choose a supplier (beyond price)
sections.html:
• Customer service: Citizens Advice publishes a regular ranking of suppliers on complaints, call waiting times and billing accuracy.
  • The tariff, not the brand: the same supplier can be cheap on one tariff and expensive on another. Compare tariff types first.
  • Smart and EV features: if you have an electric car, battery or solar panels, the cheapest supplier is often the one with the best time-of-use or export tariff.
  • Green claims: “100% renewable” can mean the supplier buys certificates (REGOs) or buys directly from generators. Ask which.
  • Payment method: Direct Debit and prepay are cheaper than paying on receipt of a bill.

Sources: Citizens Advice: compare energy suppliers’ customer service · Citizens Advice: energy supply.

sections.h2: If something goes wrong with your supplier
sections.html: Complain to the supplier first. If it isn’t resolved within eight weeks, or you get a final response you’re unhappy with, you can take it to the free Energy Ombudsman. If your supplier goes bust, Ofgem appoints a new one and your supply continues; credit balances are protected.

faqs.q: Who is the biggest energy supplier in the UK?
faqs.a: Octopus Energy is currently the largest household energy supplier in Great Britain, with British Gas second. If E.ON completes its purchase of OVO, the combined group would be one of the largest.

faqs.q: What happens to my OVO account in the E.ON takeover?
faqs.a: Nothing changes until the deal completes. OVO and E.ON keep operating separately, existing tariffs (including fixes) are honoured, and your supply won’t be interrupted. OVO says it will contact customers well before anything changes.
No. We don’t publish paid or invented rankings. For customer service, use Citizens Advice’s supplier ranking. For price, compare tariffs for your own usage.
